schema: hackathon.so idea cards v1 (see docs/RECORD_FORMAT.md). Hand-written seed cards; no script writes this file.

ideas.title: Fridge Photo Meal Planner
ideas.pitch: Snap the inside of a fridge and get three dinners that use up what expires first.
ideas.whatItDoes: Built for flatmates and busy parents who throw food away because nobody knows what is in the fridge. One photo goes to a vision model that lists the visible ingredients, the user marks anything close to its use-by date, and the app returns three simple recipes that use those items first. A shopping list covers only what is missing. In the demo, a phone photo of a real fridge turns into three recipes on screen in under a minute.

ideas.title: Webcam Fingerspelling Tutor
ideas.pitch: Learn one sign language alphabet with a webcam that checks each hand shape as it is made.
ideas.whatItDoes: Aimed at hearing friends and relatives of deaf people who want to learn fingerspelling in one sign language, such as ASL or BSL. The browser tracks hand landmarks from the webcam, a small classifier trained on the team's own recordings recognises each letter, and a practice mode asks the learner to spell short words. Letters turn green when recognised, and the app slows down on the ones the learner keeps missing. In the demo, a judge spells their own name and watches it fill in letter by letter.

ideas.title: Alt Text Assistant for Editors
ideas.pitch: A browser extension that finds images with no alt text and drafts it for an editor to approve.
ideas.whatItDoes: Made for editors of news sites, blogs and school websites who publish images without the descriptions that screen reader users depend on. The extension scans the open page, outlines every image missing alt text, and drafts a short description with a vision model. The editor approves, edits or rejects each draft, then copies the results into their content management system. In the demo, a busy article page lights up with flagged images and three drafts are approved in a few clicks.

ideas.title: QR Check-in Attendance Tokens
ideas.pitch: Meetup attendees scan a QR code at the door and receive a non-transferable attendance token on a testnet.
ideas.whatItDoes: For meetup and club organisers who want a lightweight, verifiable record of who attended which event. The door screen shows a rotating QR code, and scanning it with a connected wallet mints a non-transferable token for that event, while the rotation stops people sharing the code online. An organiser page lists check-ins in real time and lets members show their attendance history. In the demo, three phones scan the projected code and the attendance counter ticks up live.

ideas.title: Teen Allowance Smart Wallet
ideas.pitch: A smart contract wallet where a teen spends freely up to a weekly limit and bigger payments need a parent's approval.
ideas.whatItDoes: For parents who want to give teenagers real practice with digital money without handing over full control. The contract holds a weekly allowance that the teen can spend without asking, while any payment above the limit waits for a parent to approve or decline from their own phone. Both sides see a simple history of what was spent and when. In the demo, a small payment goes through instantly and a larger one pops up on the parent's phone for approval.

ideas.title: Subscription Leak Finder
ideas.pitch: Upload a bank statement export and see every recurring charge, its yearly cost and any recent price rise.
ideas.whatItDoes: For students and young professionals who lose track of small monthly subscriptions. The user uploads a CSV export from their bank, the app groups transactions by merchant and spacing to detect recurring charges, and it totals what each one costs over a year. Charges that went up since the previous month are flagged. In the demo, a sample statement turns into a ranked list of subscriptions with the yearly total at the top.

ideas.title: Receipt Photo Bill Splitter
ideas.pitch: Scan a shared receipt, let each person tap what they had, and settle up in the fewest transfers.
ideas.whatItDoes: For flatmates and friend groups who split groceries or meals and argue about who owes what. One person photographs the receipt, OCR turns it into line items, and everyone taps the items they shared on their own phone through a link. The app then works out the smallest set of transfers that settles the bill. In the demo, a real receipt is scanned, three phones claim items, and the settle-up screen shows who pays whom.

ideas.title: Text Reminders for Older Relatives
ideas.pitch: Medication and water reminders by SMS to a basic phone, with an alert to family when nobody replies.
ideas.whatItDoes: For family carers who support an older relative who uses a basic mobile phone rather than a smartphone. The carer schedules reminders on a web page, the relative gets a text and replies with 1 to confirm, and a missed reply after a set time sends an alert to the carer. A simple calendar shows confirmed and missed reminders for the week. In the demo, a reminder reaches a phone on stage, the reply turns the dashboard green, and an ignored one triggers the carer alert.

ideas.title: Walk-in Clinic Queue Texts
ideas.pitch: Patients at a walk-in clinic get a text when they are three places from the front, so they can wait elsewhere.
ideas.whatItDoes: For small walk-in clinics with crowded waiting rooms and patients who would rather wait outside or nearby. Reception adds each patient by phone number, presses Next as people are called, and the system texts whoever is now three places away. Patients can reply to say they are running late, which moves them back one place. In the demo, the front desk presses Next and the third person in the queue gets a text on their phone.

ideas.title: Home Physio Rep Counter
ideas.pitch: A webcam app that counts physiotherapy exercise reps and flags the ones that miss the prescribed range of motion.
ideas.whatItDoes: For people doing home exercises between physiotherapy appointments who are not sure they are doing them right. Pose estimation in the browser tracks joints, counts repetitions for a chosen exercise, and checks each one against a target angle the physiotherapist sets. A weekly summary of sessions can be shared as a link. In the demo, a team member does five squats in front of a laptop and the counter flags the one that was too shallow.

ideas.title: Commute Swap Planner
ideas.pitch: Compare the time and emissions of every way to get to work and suggest one realistic swap a week.
ideas.whatItDoes: For office workers who drive every day and would switch some trips if the trade-off were clear. The user enters home and work locations, the app pulls journey options from a routing service, and it estimates emissions per option from published emission factors. Instead of a lecture it suggests one swap, such as train plus bike on one weekday, with the extra minutes and the saved emissions side by side. In the demo, a real commute is entered and the weekly swap card appears with its numbers.

ideas.title: Cafe Surplus Food Matcher
ideas.pitch: Cafes post end-of-day leftovers and nearby shelters claim them with a pickup code.
ideas.whatItDoes: For cafes and bakeries that bin good food at closing time, and for the shelters and food banks nearby. Staff post what is left and a pickup window in two taps, registered shelters within range get a notification, and the first to claim receives a pickup code. The cafe sees who is coming and when. In the demo, a cafe posts a tray of sandwiches, a shelter's phone buzzes, and the claim shows up on the cafe screen with its code.

ideas.title: Rain Barrel Level Alert
ideas.pitch: An ultrasonic sensor in a rain barrel tracks the litres collected and warns before it overflows.
ideas.whatItDoes: For gardeners and community gardens that collect rainwater and lose it when the barrel overflows in a storm. An ESP32 with an ultrasonic distance sensor measures the water level every few minutes and publishes it over MQTT. A dashboard converts the level to litres, charts what was collected, and sends a phone alert at 90 percent full. In the demo, water is poured into a bucket under the sensor and the litres rise live until the alert fires.

ideas.title: Contrast Fixer for Figma
ideas.pitch: A Figma plugin that finds text failing WCAG contrast and swaps in the nearest passing colour from the file's palette.
ideas.whatItDoes: For product designers who discover accessibility problems only after handing off a design. The plugin walks the selected frame, measures every text and background pair with the WCAG contrast formula, and lists each failure next to the closest colour from the file's own styles that passes. Applying a fix updates the layer in place. In the demo, a crowded dashboard mockup shows its failures and one click fixes them all on screen.

ideas.title: Paper Sketch to Clickable Prototype
ideas.pitch: Photograph a hand-drawn wireframe and get a clickable HTML prototype in the browser.
ideas.whatItDoes: For designers and founders who sketch screens on paper in early meetings and want to test the flow straight away. A vision model reads the photo, maps boxes and labels to standard components, and generates HTML for each screen, with arrows drawn between screens turned into links. The result can be adjusted in a simple side panel. In the demo, a login screen and a home screen are drawn on paper, photographed, and clicked through in the browser.

ideas.title: Bus Bunching Map
ideas.pitch: A live map that spots buses on the same route arriving in clumps and logs where it keeps happening.
ideas.whatItDoes: For transit riders and local advocacy groups who suspect buses arrive in pairs after long gaps. The app reads a city's public GTFS Realtime feed, measures the gap between consecutive buses on each route, and marks any pair running closer than a set threshold. A heat map shows the stops where bunching happens most across the day. In the demo, the live map highlights two buses on one route arriving within a minute of each other.

ideas.title: My Street Air Quality Story
ideas.pitch: Pick a street and see when its air is worst during the week, from public sensor data.
ideas.whatItDoes: For residents and parents who want to know when to walk to school or open the windows. The app pulls readings from the nearest public air quality sensors through the OpenAQ API and charts pollution by hour of day and day of week. A short plain language summary names the worst and best times. In the demo, a judge picks a street in their own city and sees which hour has the worst air on weekdays.

ideas.title: Standby Power Spy
ideas.pitch: Log a device's power draw through a smart plug and reveal what it costs while switched off.
ideas.whatItDoes: For households and student flats curious about how much their gadgets use on standby. A smart plug with a local HTTP API is polled every few seconds, readings are stored with timestamps, and the dashboard separates in-use power from standby power. It projects a yearly cost from a tariff the user enters. In the demo, a phone charger with no phone attached is plugged in and its standby draw appears on the live chart.
stack: a smart plug with a local HTTP API

ideas.title: Visual Alerts for Doorbell and Alarms
ideas.pitch: A small listening device that flashes a lamp and buzzes a phone when the doorbell or smoke alarm sounds.
ideas.whatItDoes: For deaf and hard of hearing people who miss the doorbell, the kettle or a smoke alarm at home. A Raspberry Pi with a USB microphone runs a pretrained audio classifier, recognises a few household sounds, and makes a smart bulb flash in a different colour for each one. A phone notification names the sound, as an extra cue next to certified alarms rather than a replacement. In the demo, a doorbell recording plays on stage and the lamp on the table flashes blue.

ideas.title: Two-Phone Co-op Puzzle
ideas.pitch: A browser puzzle game where each player's phone shows only half of the map, so they have to talk to win.
ideas.whatItDoes: For friends at a party or a pub who want a quick game that gets people talking rather than staring at screens. Each player joins a room from their phone, the server sends each one a different half of the level, and switches on one phone open doors on the other. Levels get harder as the room clears them. In the demo, two judges play the first level on their own phones while the room watches.

ideas.title: Translate to Defend
ideas.pitch: A tower defence game where typing the translation of each incoming word stops it.
ideas.whatItDoes: For language learners who find flashcards dull and want vocabulary practice that feels like a game. Words in the target language march toward the base, typing the correct translation destroys them, and words the player misses come back more often in later waves. A results screen lists the words to review. In the demo, a judge plays a sixty second Spanish wave and the end screen shows the three words they missed.

ideas.title: Official Letter Explainer
ideas.pitch: Photograph an official letter and get a short summary in the reader's own language, with the deadline and next step.
ideas.whatItDoes: For newcomers and anyone who receives tax, housing or benefits letters in a language they do not read well. A photo goes to a multimodal model that extracts the sender, what is being asked and any deadline, then writes a three line summary in the language the user picks. The original text sits underneath so nothing is hidden, and the deadline can be added to a calendar. In the demo, a sample letter from a city office is photographed and its summary appears in Spanish with the reply-by date highlighted.

ideas.title: Volunteer Shift Swap Board
ideas.pitch: Food bank volunteers swap or drop shifts by text, and coordinators see the gaps at a glance.
ideas.whatItDoes: For volunteer coordinators at food banks and community kitchens who spend hours on the phone filling gaps. Coordinators post the rota, volunteers get a personal link by text with no account to create, and anyone who cannot make a shift can offer it to the group. The first volunteer to accept takes it and the rota updates for everyone. In the demo, one volunteer offers a Saturday shift, another accepts by text, and the empty slot on the coordinator view fills in.

ideas.title: Lecture Slides to Flashcards
ideas.pitch: Turn a lecture PDF into question and answer flashcards that link back to the slide they came from.
ideas.whatItDoes: For students revising for exams from long lecture decks. The app extracts text from each slide, asks a language model for a few question and answer pairs per slide, and keeps the slide number with every card. Students quiz themselves in the browser or export the cards to Anki. In the demo, a real lecture deck is uploaded, a quiz starts, and a wrong answer opens the exact slide that explains it.

ideas.title: Group Project Contribution Tracker
ideas.pitch: A weekly summary of who did what in a student team's GitHub repository, so problems surface early.
ideas.whatItDoes: For students in group projects where one person ends up doing most of the work and nobody notices until the deadline. The team connects its GitHub repository, and the app counts commits, pull requests opened and reviewed, and issues closed per person each week. A short weekly summary is posted to the team's chat. In the demo, a real repository is connected and a chart shows each member's contributions for the past week.

ideas.title: Free Study Room Finder
ideas.pitch: Students scan a QR code on a study room door to mark it free or taken, and a campus map shows what is open.
ideas.whatItDoes: For students who walk from building to building looking for an empty study room. Each room door gets a printed QR code, scanning it marks the room free or taken, and claims expire after a set time so the map does not go stale. A campus map shows which rooms are free right now. In the demo, a judge scans a printed code and that room turns green on the projected map.

ideas.title: Incident Timeline Bot for Slack
ideas.pitch: A Slack bot that turns an incident channel into a draft postmortem timeline.
ideas.whatItDoes: For on-call engineers who spend the day after an outage reconstructing what happened from scrollback. When an incident channel is closed, the bot collects its messages, alert posts and deploy notices, orders them by time, and asks a language model to draft a timeline with key decisions marked. The draft is posted back as a document for the team to correct. In the demo, a scripted incident is replayed in a test workspace and the bot posts a clean timeline.

ideas.title: Contract Renewal Radar
ideas.pitch: Upload vendor contracts and get calendar reminders before each one renews automatically.
ideas.whatItDoes: For office managers at small businesses who get caught by contracts that renew automatically. The user uploads PDF contracts, a language model extracts the renewal date, notice period and cancellation method, and each answer is shown next to the clause it came from. The app then exports cancel-by reminders as a calendar file. In the demo, three sample contracts are uploaded and their cancel-by dates appear on a calendar with the source clauses highlighted.

ideas.title: Neighbourhood Tool Library
ideas.pitch: Neighbours list tools they rarely use, and others borrow them with a request and a return date.
ideas.whatItDoes: For neighbours who each own a drill or a ladder that sits unused most of the year. Owners list items with a photo, borrowers request a date range, and the owner approves by replying to a text message. Reminders go out the day before an item is due back. In the demo, a drill is listed, a second phone requests it, and the owner's approval shows the drill as on loan.

ideas.title: Lost Property Photo Matcher
ideas.pitch: Staff photograph found items, and owners describe what they lost in words to find a match.
ideas.whatItDoes: For gyms, libraries and venues with a box of lost property that nobody can search. Staff photograph each found item, and image embeddings are stored with the date and place it was found. Owners type a description, such as a black umbrella with a wooden handle, and text to image similarity ranks the closest matches. In the demo, a judge describes an item from the box and its photo comes up first.
